answer:
Headline results for run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (PoroTomo DAS, Brady Hot Springs, March 2016):

DATA SCOPE
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the time window).
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above the catalogue completeness magnitude Mc).
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days (net extraction).
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016).

CALIBRATED PROBABILITY (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5; magnitudes from the LBNL catalogue, so this is the calibrated estimate):
  b      Sigma      P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.00   -5.449     0.0001198      5.236e-06                        0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922       0.0002155                        0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474        0.0006484                        0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated DAS magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842.

INTERPRETATION
- The calibrated (LBNL catalogue) probabilities are the ones to trust: P(Mw>=5.5) per year ranges from ~1.2e-4 (b=1.0) to ~1.5e-2 (b=0.65) — a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is very unlikely per year under the calibrated model.
- The DAS-based number (P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842, Sigma = -2.698) is an upper bound only: DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and all 62 detections are treated as events at/above Mc, so it systematically over-counts and should not be read as a calibrated hazard probability.
